pr_title: Errors from cgroup destroy are swallowed. Log error at warning level.
pr_body:
**What type of PR is this?**
/kind cleanup

**What this PR does / why we need it**:
Housekeeping sync loop finds an orphaned pod and tries to clean it up. The removal of the kubepod slice may fail. This leads to the docker scope timing out and entering a failed state. The returned error(s) from runc are swallowed making debugging difficult.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:
Fixes #84595

**Special notes for your reviewer**:

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?**:
```release-note
NONE
```

**Additional documentation e.g., KEPs (Kubernetes Enhancement Proposals), usage docs, etc.**:
```docs
```

issue_context.title: Errors returned from pod_container_manager_linux Destroy to remove a pods cgroup are swallowed
issue_context.body:
**What happened**:

Housekeeping sync loop finds an orphaned pod and tries to clean it up. The kubepod slice, as seen below, is not removed by `cleanupOrphanedPodCgroups -> go pcm.Destroy(val)` with no indication as to why. This leads to the docker scope timing out and entering a failed state. The returned error(s) from runc are swallowed making debugging difficult.

```
Oct 16 21:18:26 server atomic-openshift-node: I1016 21:18:26.531606    1694 kubelet.go:1907] SyncLoop (housekeeping)
Oct 16 21:18:26 server atomic-openshift-node: I1016 21:18:26.670054    1694 kubelet_pods.go:1082] Killing unwanted pod "test-cron-three-1571285880-bb"
Oct 16 21:18:26 server atomic-openshift-node: I1016 21:18:26.792307    1694 kubelet_pods.go:1682] Orphaned pod "20f666f1-f095-11e9-916f-0050568379a2" found, removing pod cgroups
Oct 16 21:18:26 server systemd: Stopping libcontainer container 4396d3ff70201d494fa265e1966435288d6806acb99f0d601bf56f8804f79a24.
Oct 16 21:19:57 server systemd: docker-4396d3ff70201d494fa265e1966435288d6806acb99f0d601bf56f8804f79a24.scope stopping timed out. Killing.
Oct 16 21:19:57 server systemd: Stopped libcontainer container 4396d3ff70201d494fa265e1966435288d6806acb99f0d601bf56f8804f79a24.
Oct 16 21:19:57 server systemd: Unit docker-4396d3ff70201d494fa265e1966435288d6806acb99f0d601bf56f8804f79a24.scope entered failed state.
```


**What you expected to happen**:
As per other areas of the sync loop, useful errors are logged at debug level due to the async calls.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
N/A

**Anything else we need to know?**:
N/A

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): master

@tedyu yes, definitely looked! In this specific situation, the pods are never retried.

What we see happen with these pods:

ADD -> RECONCILE -> Started Volumes -> Created slice -> No sandbox for pod -> Started libcontainer -> ContainerStarted -> ContainerStarted -> RECONSILE -> ContainerDied -> RECONCILE -> Unmounts -> Killing unwanted pod -> Orphaned removing pod cgroups -> container kill failed because of 'container not found' or 'no such process' -> cleanup: failed to unmount secrets -> ContainerDied -> Container garbage collection succeeded -> SyncLoop (SYNC): 141 pods (including this one) -> stopping timed out. Killing. -> Stopped libcontainer -> Removed slice -> DELETE -> REMOVE -> err: pod not found

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_pods.go#L1714

Destroy all cgroups of the pod that should not be running, by first killing all the attached processes to these cgroups. We ignore errors thrown by the method, as the housekeeping loop would again try to delete these unwanted pod cgroups

Despite running, the slice is not removed and we do not log or indicate why. Subsequently, the pod is NOT determined to be either an active pod or for some reason not in the cgroup list that is passed into kl.cleanupOrphanedPodCgroups(cgroupPods, activePods) during housekeeping loops.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_pods.go#L1064

A more detailed look, which I believe is accurate ;):

housekeepingCh -> HandlePodCleanups -> cgroupPods=UID+CGroupName=GetAllPodsFromCgroups -> allPods=GetPodsAndMirrorPods -> activePods=filterOutTerminatedPods -> cleanupOrphanedPodCgroups

I do not think desiredPods and runningPods are relevant here..

So either:

a) the pod is not found and added to allPods (seems unlikely) but we can't know for sure..

b) the pod is incorrectly determined to be active via activePods which again we can not determine..

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/54a30700a38452a5113adcfba0f98adcc5e05f2d/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_pods.go#L1014
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/54a30700a38452a5113adcfba0f98adcc5e05f2d/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_pods.go#L960
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/54a30700a38452a5113adcfba0f98adcc5e05f2d/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_pods.go#L869

Any pod that is not Failed, Succeeded or has a DeletionTimestamp set and a status of Terminated or Waiting - anything else returns false and is deemed active

c) the pod cgroup is not found in m.subsystems.MountPoints and added to cgroupPods - unlikely, but could be a bug but the root of this issue is the fact that all of the scopes and slices exist and keep building up until things start failing...

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/54a30700a38452a5113adcfba0f98adcc5e05f2d/pkg/kubelet/cm/pod_container_manager_linux.go#L237

GetAllPodsFromCgroups could use some logging... Maybe a V 5 log that prints out foundPods at the end...


From there, they're passed into the cleanup: kl.cleanupOrphanedPodCgroups(cgroupPods, activePods)
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/54a30700a38452a5113adcfba0f98adcc5e05f2d/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_pods.go#L1064

1) All activePod UIDs are put into a podSet

2) A range loop of uid and cgroup name from cgroupPods looks to see if the uid from cgroupPods also exists in the podSet (active pods)

3) If the uid from cgroupPods exists in the podSet we skip out of the loop

4) If it doesn't, the pod is orphaned (not active w/ cgroups on the filesystem) and we call pcm.Destroy(val) on the cgroup name.

Doesn't make sense why pcm.Destroy(val) ignores errors... it would be helpful!

tryKillingCgroupProcesses logs any error and also returns the an error which is always swallowed.. we don't see any issues here
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/54a30700a38452a5113adcfba0f98adcc5e05f2d/pkg/kubelet/cm/pod_container_manager_linux.go#L190

More problematic, the call to cgroupManager.Destroy only returns an error which would be swallowed... Could probably use a similar level 3 log here like what you have for  tryKillingCgroupProcesses because as you can see, were totally blind here...

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/54a30700a38452a5113adcfba0f98adcc5e05f2d/pkg/kubelet/cm/pod_container_manager_linux.go#L199

@tedyu your change is of a similar nature to what I proposed in my PR for this issue, just a level higher. I think there are a few areas noted above the could help further debug this.. Still haven't been able to get my PR merged with additional logging.

The following code was relatively new (compared to when you logged this issue):
```
	containersTerminal = notRunning(status.ContainerStatuses)
	// The kubelet must accept config changes from the pod spec until it has reached a point where changes would
	// have no effect on any running container.
	podWorkerTerminal = status.Phase == v1.PodFailed || status.Phase == v1.PodSucceeded || (pod.DeletionTimestamp != nil && containersTerminal)
```

Indeed... I looked into it a while ago and those changes are new via: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/88440 - Could definitely make a different if the issue is related to pod getting filtered out from activePods when they have not been fully cleaned up yet on the subsequent housekeeping syncloop runs.
@tedyu I think 88440 is promising, but I still think it makes sense to add some logging here. Do you want want to proceed with my open PR, your suggestion in kubelet_pods.go or both?
You can proceed with your PR.

review_comments:
@tedyu I don't feel super strongly, but one advantage of logging this using `klog.V(3).Infof` would be that it is consistent with the logging statement on line 190. I don't have a ton of context on this part of the code base, but I do get the sense they are describing equally bad failure states... in other words, it seems sensible to me that they'd have the same log level.

Alternatively, I suppose we could change both to be a `Warning`.

@mattjmcnaughton that was my initial rational around consistency. I believe this error and a number of others logged at debug are generally ok to ignore as they should be self-resolving through subsequent sync loops. You would probable only want to see them when you find a definitive problem case (like what I am trying to root cause).
Gotcha! So just to be sure we're on the same page, are you planning on changing it to `klog.V(3).Infof`? Or is there a reason more important than consistency for it to be `klog.Warningf`?

@mattjmcnaughton In the original PR I had it at v3 info and per the discussion with @tedyu I changed it to warn. I am on the side of having it an v3 info and am happy to change it back it everyone is happy with that per my explanation.
@tedyu what do you think? I vote `klog.V(3).Infof` :)
Looking at the log on line 190, I think it should be warning as well:)
